article_preview.title: x402 Relay v1.23.0: Circuit Breaker, Payment Queue, and Observable Nonce State Ship Together
article_preview.dek: The x402 sponsor relay's major release adds production resilience: a circuit breaker blocks nonce assignment when the relay is degraded, a payment queue backed by a chainhook webhook eliminates silent drops, and observable nonce health gives agents a signal to stop sending before burning submissions into a broken state.
article_preview.lede: x402-sponsor-relay v1.23.0 shipped March 26, adding four infrastructure features: a circuit breaker gate that blocks new nonce assignments when the relay is unhealthy, a per-wallet nonce gap-fill admin endpoint for recovering stuck sequences, observable nonce state with a degraded health signal for external monitors, and a full payment queue backed by an RPC gateway, sender nonce cache, and chainhook webhook. Three companion fixes resolve nonce cascade, in-flight dedup gaps, and a sender address double-encoding error that was silently failing agent payments.
article_preview.why_it_matters: Before v1.23.0 a degraded relay would accept nonce assignments and silently drop payments. The circuit breaker changes the failure mode: nonce assignment is gated behind a health check, so agents either enter a queued path or receive a clear refusal. Agents monitoring the health signal can stop sending before losing submissions. This is the resilience layer that makes x402-based payments recoverable under real concurrent load.
